cards.title: Fixed Geographical Direction of Prayer (Qiblah) and Shift from Jerusalem
cards.note: Surah 2:142–145 transitions the community from praying toward Jerusalem to facing the Meccan sanctuary, building on the biblical and rabbinic law of facing Jerusalem in Daniel 6:10, Mishnah Berakhot 4:5, and Talmud Berakhot 30a.

discussion.view: Traditional commentators state that praying toward Jerusalem was a temporary divine command in Medina to test who would follow the Prophet, before God restored the primordial Abrahamic sanctuary in Mecca as the permanent direction of prayer.
discussion.reply: Fixing daily prayer toward Jerusalem and its Temple is anchored in 1 Kings 8:44–48, Daniel 6:10, Mishnah Berakhot 4:5 (~AD 200), and Talmud Berakhot 30a (~AD 500). Adopting the Jerusalem prayer orientation upon arriving among Medinan Jewish tribes, and shifting to the Meccan sanctuary roughly sixteen months later after Jewish rejection, tracks the historical realignment of the Medinan polity.

cards.quranEn: [142] The fools among the people will say, ‘What has turned them from the direction (of prayer) which they were (facing) toward?’ Say: ‘The East and the West (belong) to God. He guides whomever He pleases to a straight path.’ [143] In this way We have made you a community (in the) middle, so that you may be witnesses over the people, and that the messenger may be a witness over you. And We established the direction (of prayer) which you were (facing) toward only so that We might know the one who would follow the messenger from the one who would turn back on his heels. Surely it was hard indeed, except for those whom God guided. But God was not one to let your belief go to waste. Surely God is indeed kind (and) compassionate with the people. [144] We do see you turning your face about in the sky, and We shall indeed turn you in a direction which you will be pleased with. Turn your face in the direction of the Sacred Mosque, and wherever you are, turn your faces in its direction. Surely those who have been given the Book know indeed that it is the truth from their Lord. God is not oblivious of what they do. [145] Yet even if you bring every sign to those who have been given the Book, they will not follow your direction. You are not a follower of their direction, nor are they followers of each other’s direction. If indeed you follow their (vain) desires, after the knowledge which has come to you, surely then you will indeed be among the evildoers.
quranHighlights: What has turned them from the direction (of prayer) which they were (facing) toward?
Turn your face in the direction of the Sacred Mosque, and wherever you are, turn your faces in its direction

sources.title: Mishnah Berakhot 4:5
sources.en: While praying, one must face toward the direction of the Holy Temple. One who was riding on a donkey should dismount and pray calmly. If he is unable to dismount, he should turn his face toward the direction of the Temple. If he is unable to turn his face, it is sufficient that he focus his heart opposite the Holy of Holies.
highlights: While praying, one must face toward the direction of the Holy Temple
he should turn his face toward the direction of the Temple

sources.en: One who was standing in prayer in the Diaspora should focus his heart toward Eretz Yisrael, as it is stated: “And they shall pray to You by way of their land which You have given to their fathers” (I Kings 8:48). One who was standing in Eretz Yisrael should focus his heart toward Jerusalem, as it is stated: “And they shall pray to the Lord by way of the city that You have chosen” (I Kings 8:44). One who was standing in the Temple should focus his heart toward the Holy of Holies, as it is stated: “And they shall pray toward this place” (I Kings 8:35).

cards.quranAr: ۞سَيَقُولُ ٱلسُّفَهَآءُ مِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ مَا وَلَّىٰهُمۡ عَن قِبۡلَتِهِمُ ٱلَّتِي كَانُواْ عَلَيۡهَاۚ قُل لِّلَّهِ ٱلۡمَشۡرِقُ وَٱلۡمَغۡرِبُۚ يَهۡدِي مَن يَشَآءُ إِلَىٰ صِرَٰطٖ مُّسۡتَقِيمٖ ﴿142﴾ وَكَذَٰلِكَ جَعَلۡنَٰكُمۡ أُمَّةٗ وَسَطٗا لِّتَكُونُواْ شُهَدَآءَ عَلَى ٱلنَّاسِ وَيَكُونَ ٱلرَّسُولُ عَلَيۡكُمۡ شَهِيدٗاۗ وَمَا جَعَلۡنَا ٱلۡقِبۡلَةَ ٱلَّتِي كُنتَ عَلَيۡهَآ إِلَّا لِنَعۡلَمَ مَن يَتَّبِعُ ٱلرَّسُولَ مِمَّن يَنقَلِبُ عَلَىٰ عَقِبَيۡهِۚ وَإِن كَانَتۡ لَكَبِيرَةً إِلَّا عَلَى ٱلَّذِينَ هَدَى ٱللَّهُۗ وَمَا كَانَ ٱللَّهُ لِيُضِيعَ إِيمَٰنَكُمۡۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ بِٱلنَّاسِ لَرَءُوفٞ رَّحِيمٞ ﴿143﴾ قَدۡ نَرَىٰ تَقَلُّبَ وَجۡهِكَ فِي ٱلسَّمَآءِۖ فَلَنُوَلِّيَنَّكَ قِبۡلَةٗ تَرۡضَىٰهَاۚ فَوَلِّ وَجۡهَكَ شَطۡرَ ٱلۡمَسۡجِدِ ٱلۡحَرَامِۚ وَحَيۡثُ مَا كُنتُمۡ فَوَلُّواْ وُجُوهَكُمۡ شَطۡرَهُۥۗ وَإِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُواْ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ لَيَعۡلَمُونَ أَنَّهُ ٱلۡحَقُّ مِن رَّبِّهِمۡۗ وَمَا ٱللَّهُ بِغَٰفِلٍ عَمَّا يَعۡمَلُونَ ﴿144﴾ وَلَئِنۡ أَتَيۡتَ ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُواْ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ بِكُلِّ ءَايَةٖ مَّا تَبِعُواْ قِبۡلَتَكَۚ وَمَآ أَنتَ بِتَابِعٖ قِبۡلَتَهُمۡۚ وَمَا بَعۡضُهُم بِتَابِعٖ قِبۡلَةَ بَعۡضٖۚ وَلَئِنِ ٱتَّبَعۡتَ أَهۡوَآءَهُم مِّنۢ بَعۡدِ مَا جَآءَكَ مِنَ ٱلۡعِلۡمِ إِنَّكَ إِذٗا لَّمِنَ ٱلظَّـٰلِمِينَ ﴿145﴾

cards.title: Fourfold Dietary Prohibition and the Life-Saving Necessity Exemption
cards.note: Surah 2:173 forbids carrion, blood, swine flesh, and idol-dedicated meat while exempting those forced by life-saving necessity, combining Acts 15:28–29, Leviticus 11:7–8, and Talmud Yoma 82a (pikuach nefesh).

discussion.view: Islamic theology regards the prohibition of carrion, blood, pork, and idol-consecrated meat—paired with mercy for one forced by starvation—as the original prophetic dietary law perfected in the Quran.
discussion.reply: Whereas the Mosaic Torah lists dozens of forbidden land, sea, and winged creatures in Leviticus 11, the compact fourfold list of idol-sacrificed meat, blood, carrion/strangled animals, and pork reproduces the Apostolic Decree of Acts 15:28–29 as observed by Late Antique Eastern Christians, combined with the rabbinic life-saving necessity exemption (pikuach nefesh) codified in Talmud Yoma 82a.

cards.quranEn: He has only forbidden to you: the dead (animal), and the blood, and swine’s flesh, and what has been dedicated to (a god) other than God. But whoever is forced (by necessity), not desiring or (deliberately) transgressing – no sin (rests) on him. Surely God is forgiving, compassionate.
quranHighlights: the dead (animal), and the blood, and swine’s flesh, and what has been dedicated to (a god) other than God
But whoever is forced (by necessity), not desiring or (deliberately) transgressing – no sin (rests) on him

cards.title: Ritual Ablution (Wudu'): Washing Face, Forearms, Head, and Feet Before Prayer
cards.note: Surah 5:6 codifies the four-part pre-prayer ablution (washing face and forearms to elbows, wiping head and feet to ankles) and dry soil wiping (tayammum), paralleling Exodus 30:19–21 and Talmud Bavli Berakhot 15a.

discussion.view: Sunni and Shi'i jurists treat Surah 5:6 as the comprehensive Medinan charter for minor ritual ablution (wudu'), major ritual bathing (ghusl), and dry earth purification (tayammum) prior to canonical prayer.
discussion.reply: Washing the hands and feet with water before approaching sacred service is commanded in Exodus 30:19–21, and Talmud Bavli Berakhot 15a (~AD 500) extends this priestly washing to every layperson after relieving oneself before reciting the Shema and Amidah—adding the exact rabbinic rule that one lacking water wipes the hands with earth or a pebble.

cards.quranEn: You who believe! When you stand up for the prayer, wash your faces and your hands up to the elbows, and wipe your heads and your feet up to the ankles. If you are defiled, purify yourselves. If you are sick or on a journey, or if one of you has come from the toilet, or if you have touched women, and you do not find any water, take clean earth and wipe your faces and your hands with it. God does not wish to place any difficulty on you, but He wishes to purify you and to complete His blessing on you, so that you may be thankful.
quranHighlights: When you stand up for the prayer, wash your faces and your hands up to the elbows, and wipe your heads and your feet up to the ankles

sources.title: Talmud Bavli Berakhot
sources.ref: Berakhot 15a (Washing Hands Before Prayer or Wiping with Earth)
sources.en: Anyone who relieves himself, washes his hands, dons phylacteries, recites Shema, and prays, the verse ascribes credit to him as if he built an altar and offered a sacrifice upon it, as it is written: “I will wash in purity my hands, and I will encircle the altar of the Lord” (Psalms 26:6). Rava said to him: Do you not maintain, Master, that one who does so, it is as if he immersed his entire body, as it is written: “I will wash in purity,” and it is not written: “I will wash my hands”? Ravina said to Rava: My Master, look at this Torah scholar [tzurva merabbanan] who came from Eretz Yisrael and said something astonishing: One who has no water with which to wash his hands, it is sufficient that he wipes his hands with earth, a rock, or a sliver of wood.
highlights: Anyone who relieves himself, washes his hands, dons phylacteries, recites Shema, and prays

cards.title: Dietary Code: Carrion, Blood, Pork, Strangled Meat, and Divination Arrows
cards.note: Surah 5:3 expands the fourfold dietary ban with strangled, beaten, fallen, gored, and beast-torn animals alongside meat sacrificed on pagan stones and divination arrows, combining the Apostolic Decree of Acts 15:19–20 and the beast-torn flesh ban of Exodus 22:31.

discussion.view: Muslim scholars view Surah 5:3, revealed during the Farewell Pilgrimage period, as the final completion of Islamic dietary law prohibiting both unslaughtered animals and pagan sacrificial and divinatory rites.
discussion.reply: Surah 5:3 brings together three distinct Near Eastern legal strata: the Apostolic Decree's ban on idol-offerings, blood, and strangled meat (Acts 15:19–20), the Torah prohibition on eating animals torn by wild beasts unless properly slaughtered (Exodus 22:31), and the pre-Islamic Arabian practice of partitioning camel meat with divination arrows (azlam) beside sacrificial stones (ansab).

cards.quranEn: Forbidden to you (to eat) are: the dead (animal), and the blood, and swine’s flesh, and what has been dedicated to (a god) other than God, and the strangled (to death), and the beaten (to death), and the fallen (to death), and the gored (to death), and what a wild animal has devoured – except what you have slaughtered – and what has been sacrificed on stones. And (it is forbidden) that you should divide by divination arrows – that is wickedness for you. Today those who disbelieve have no hope of (ever destroying) your religion. So do not fear them, but fear Me. Today I have perfected your religion for you, and I have completed My blessing on you, and I have approved Islam for you as a religion. But if anyone is forced by hunger, without intending to sin – surely God is forgiving, compassionate.
quranHighlights: Forbidden to you (to eat) are: the dead (animal), and the blood, and swine’s flesh, and what has been dedicated to (a god) other than God, and the strangled (to death)

cards.title: Prescribed Fasting with Make-Up Days for Sickness or Travel
cards.note: Surah 2:183–185 prescribes fasting 'as it was prescribed for those before you' and allows the sick or travelers to make up missed days later, combining Numbers 9:10–11, Mishnah Yoma 8:5, and pre-Islamic 'Ashura fasting in Bukhari 4504.

discussion.view: Muslim exegetes state that God prescribed fasting for earlier prophetic communities and transitioned the Muslim community from the earlier fast of 'Ashura to the month of Ramadan with merciful exemptions for illness and travel.
discussion.reply: Surah 2:183 explicitly appeals to the precedent of earlier communities ('as it was prescribed for those who were before you'). Its rule allowing a traveler to postpone the fast to an equal count of later days mirrors the Second Passover travel-postponement law of Numbers 9:10–11, combined with the illness exemption of Mishnah Yoma 8:5 and the pre-Islamic/Jewish 'Ashura fast in Sahih al-Bukhari 4504.

cards.quranEn: [183] You who believe! Fasting is prescribed for you, as it was prescribed for those who were before you, so that you may guard (yourselves). [184] (Fast for) a number of days. Whoever of you is sick or on a journey, (let him fast) a certain number of other days. And for those who can afford it, (there is) a ransom: feeding a poor person. Whoever does good voluntarily – it is better for him. But to fast is better for you, if (only) you knew. [185] The month of Ramaḍān, in which the Qur’ān was sent down as a guidance for the people, and as clear signs of the guidance and the Deliverance: so whoever of you is present during the month, let him fast in it, but whoever of you is sick or on a journey, (let him fast) a certain number of other days. God wishes to make it easy for you, and does not wish any hardship for you. And (He wishes) that you should fulfill the number (of days), and that you should magnify God for having guided you, and that you should be thankful.
quranHighlights: Fasting is prescribed for you, as it was prescribed for those who were before you
Whoever of you is sick or on a journey, (let him fast) a certain number of other days

cards.title: Establishing Prayer at the Two Ends of the Day and Approaches of Night
cards.note: Surah 11:114 enjoins performing ritual prayer (al-salat) 'at the two ends of the day and at the approach of the night,' mirroring the three daily prayer times in Talmud Bavli Berakhot 26b and Psalm 55:17 (LXX 54:17).

discussion.view: Commentators interpret 'the two ends of the day' as the dawn and afternoon prayers and 'the approaches of the night' as the evening and night prayers, seeing the Meccan verse as an early stage of the five daily prayers.
discussion.reply: Before the five-prayer schedule was formalized in later tradition, Surah 11:114 describes a three-part daily liturgical cycle—morning, late afternoon, and early night—that corresponds directly to the three daily prayers (evening, morning, and afternoon) of Psalm 55:17 (LXX 54:17) and Talmud Bavli Berakhot 26b.

cards.quranEn: And observe the prayer at the two ends of the day and at the approach of the night. Surely good (deeds) take away evil (ones). That is a reminder to the mindful.
quranHighlights: observe the prayer at the two ends of the day and at the approach of the night

sources.title: Talmud Bavli Berakhot 26b (Three Daily Prayers Instituted by the Patriarchs)
sources.workSub: Three Daily Prayers Instituted by the Patriarchs
sources.en: Why did the Rabbis say that the morning prayer may be recited until noon? Because, although the daily morning offering is typically brought early in the morning, it may be sacrificed until noon. And Rabbi Yehuda says: My opinion, that the morning prayer may be recited until four hours into the day, is because the daily morning offering is sacrificed until four hours. And why did the Rabbis say that the afternoon prayer may be recited until the evening? Because the daily afternoon offering is sacrificed until the evening. Rabbi Yehuda says that the afternoon prayer may be recited only until the midpoint of the afternoon because, according to his opinion, the daily afternoon offering is sacrificed until the midpoint of the afternoon. And why did they say that the evening prayer is not fixed? Because the burning of the limbs and fats of the offerings that were not consumed by the fire on the altar until the evening.
highlights: the morning prayer may be recited until noon
the afternoon prayer may be recited until the evening
the evening prayer is not fixed
